name: Manillen
description: Manillen is a popular point-trick card game played extensively in West Flanders, Belgium. Derived from the French game Manille (which came from Spanish Malilla), it features the unique 'Manille' (10) as the highest card in each suit. The game is known for its simple rules but deep strategic possibilities, especially the 'Ik ga mee' (I go along) doubling mechanic.

history.origins: Originated as a French game called Manille, derived from the Spanish game Malilla or Manilla. The term 'Manille' refers to the highest card (10) of each suit.
timeline: Spanish origins: Malilla/Manilla games from Spain
French adaptation: Manille becomes popular in France
Belgian evolution: Manillen develops in West Flanders with unique local rules
Present: One of the most popular card games in West Flanders, played in cafes and competitions
history.cultural: A social institution in West Flanders, often played in pubs (cafes) for friendly competition. Tournaments commonly play best of three 'boams' (games to 101 points).
history.evolution: The Belgian variant developed distinctive features like the 'Ik ga mee' doubling convention and the dealer's partner not looking at cards before trump selection.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, sitting across from each other. Variations exist for 2 and 6 players.
setup.deck: 32 cards (7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace in each suit). Ranking: 10 (Manille) > Ace > King > Queen > Jack > 9 > 8 > 7.
setup.dealing: To determine first dealer: each player takes a pile of cards; highest bottom card deals. Dealer shuffles (max twice), player to dealer's right cuts. Deal clockwise in batches of 3-2-3 (8 cards each). Dealer's partner must NOT look at cards before trump is chosen.

rules.objective: Be the first team to collect 101 points or more. One game to 101 is called a 'boam' (tree).
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's left leads. Must follow suit if able. If an opponent is winning, you must beat their card if possible when following suit. If void, must trump if possible (unless partner is winning).
keyRules: Must follow suit if able. If opponent is winning, must beat their card when following suit or overtrump when void; if partner is winning, no obligation to beat or trump.
Undertrumpping is illegal (cannot play a lower trump than the one winning the trick unless only small trumps left).
Dealer chooses trump (or no trump for double); no bidding. Dealer's partner must not look at cards before trump is chosen.

First team to 101 points wins one boam. Card points: 10=5, A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1; 9/8/7=0. Team with more points in tricks scores (total minus 30); doubles apply for no trump, Ik ga mee, tie, or all tricks.

strategy.basic: Lead a Manille (10) of a non-trump suit early - it will likely 'go round' (laten rondgoan) as no one can beat it without trumping. Save your trumps for when you need to win crucial tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Create voids (renoang) by discarding your only card of a suit on a trick your partner is winning. This allows you to trump when that suit is led. Avoid being stuck with an 'blooten aas' (lone Ace) - an Ace without other cards of that suit, which is vulnerable to being trumped.
strategy.advanced: Count cards carefully - this is essential in Manillen. Track which Manilles and Aces have been played. If you know all trumps are gone, your plain suit cards become more valuable. Use 'vet'n' (fattening) - playing high value cards on your partner's winning trick to capture those points safely.
tips: The 'Boeketje Vlaanderen' (Little Flemish Bouquet) - having 2 cards of every suit - is the hardest hand for choosing trumps
Remember: 10s are the highest cards, not Aces!
If you have many trumps, consider playing no trump (muulen) for the double score
Pay attention to the 'Ik ga mee' - it often indicates the opponent has a strong hand in the trump suit

variations.name: Obligatory muuls
variations.description: Each partnership must declare two no-trumps (muulen) and two blind no-trumps (blènde muul) per boam. Makes the game more exciting but shorter.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule forces two muulen and two blènde muul per boam; no engine constant overrides in schema.

variations.name: Signalling penalty
variations.description: If a partnership is caught signalling or cheating, they lose the deal and 20 points are given to the other team.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: House rule for cheating; penalty only, no engine overrides.

variations.name: Boerecoarte redeal
variations.description: Some players redeal when a player has a boerecoarte or boerinnecoarte: a hand with one Jack (zot) and five 0-point cards (7s, 8s, 9s - klintjes).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional redeal condition; no engine overrides in schema.

variations.name: Two- or six-player variants
variations.description: Two-player: dummy hands or face-up table cards; six-player: two teams of three, five cards each, two face up on table. Same trump and scoring rules.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Player count and deal differ; overrides to be added when implementing.

scoring.description: Each team counts card points in tricks won. Team with more points scores (their total minus 30); doubles apply (no trump, Ik ga mee, Ik ga tegen, tie, or all tricks). First team to 101 or more wins the boam.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 101 points or more wins one boam (game). Tournament play is often best of three boams.
